issue_context.title: replace klog.Fatal and os.Exit for defer funcs
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

Hello, team 👋

#### What happened:

The defer function will not be called if os.Exit(1).
https://play.golang.org/p/f7IjXeb62dd

> deferred functions are not run.
https://golang.org/pkg/os/#Exit

Now, the entry points of some Kubernetes components use defer functions to flush logs.

For example, kube-scheduler
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-scheduler/scheduler.go#L41
```
func main() {
	rand.Seed(time.Now().UnixNano())

	pflag.CommandLine.SetNormalizeFunc(cliflag.WordSepNormalizeFunc)

	command := app.NewSchedulerCommand()

	logs.InitLogs()
	defer logs.FlushLogs()

	if err := command.Execute(); err != nil {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

When `command.Execute()` returns an error, logs are not flushed. Is this an expected behavior?

#### How to fix

We can ensure that `defer` is executed by separating the functions as follows.

```
func main() {
  if err := realmain(); err != nil {
    os.Exit(1)
  }
}

func realmain() error {
	rand.Seed(time.Now().UnixNano())

	pflag.CommandLine.SetNormalizeFunc(cliflag.WordSepNormalizeFunc)

	command := app.NewSchedulerCommand()

	logs.InitLogs()
	defer logs.FlushLogs()

	if err := command.Execute(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
       return nil
}
```

can I pick this issue? 
/assign


## Edit (October 23)

For entry points, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105076 resolves the issue. 
But it is better to delete all klog.Fatal and os.Exit as much as possible. 
They can be replaced by returning error/nil. And in some case, we may be able to use panic() (defer funcs are executed when panic [ref](https://go.dev/blog/defer-panic-and-recover))

This is great. Happy to see all those `os.Exit()` calls removed.

There is at least one more thing that calls `os.Exit()` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dac94e1c9ee31034d174815e287ba39fa67b2b72/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/util/helpers.go#L114-L116. It's used in a lot of places, such as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dac94e1c9ee31034d174815e287ba39fa67b2b72/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/logs/logs.go#L157-L159.

Changed the issue title to easily understand the current purpose of this issue - delete all klog.Fatal and os.Exit for defer funcs.

> So, now, we only have to delete os.Exit on cobra commands for this issue

In the past I've said this, but I think we need to eliminate replace all os.Exit and klog.Fatal(it call os.Exit internally) 😓 , not just the ones on cobra commands.
We have to investigate all the places using them.

We also have to consider how to prevent them in the future. If we delete all of them, I think someone will use them again in the future.

We can forbid os.Exit and klog.Fatal with forbidgo linter (we can use this from golangci-lint), but whether or not to ban it completely needs to be discussed. Banning it completely may be overkill, but I haven't come up with any other good ideas for now.
https://golangci-lint.run/usage/linters/#forbidigo
The lease/leader election use of os.Exit is deliberate and has been baked into several controllers. We can't remove it till we have an alternate way to ensure we don't have competing controllers.

/remove-kind bug
/kind cleanup

> The lease/leader election use of os.Exit is deliberate and has been baked into several controllers. We can't remove it till we have an alternate way to ensure we don't have competing controllers.

Yes. I think there are places where `os.Exit` is definitely needed. If we were to introduce linter, we would need to use nolint comment-directive there.
https://golangci-lint.run/usage/false-positives/#nolint-directive

It is difficult to make all developers aware of the need to avoid using `os.Exit`, but, linter is one of the solutions. Hopefully, developers will avoid using `os.Exit` as much as possible and use nolint only when necessary.

And, I just found that the latest forbidigo provides the useful feature; custom forbid reason messages.
https://github.com/ashanbrown/forbidigo/pull/11

So, if golangci-lint updates its dependencies, we can use this feature and show error message like: 
`Please avoid using os.Exit as much as possible. see #102231 for more details. If you still think we need to use os.Exit here, you can use "//nolint:forbidigo // reason" here to avoid this lint issue.`
/cc @thockin

So, to sum up, I would propose this migration plan:
- find where `os.Exit` or `klog.Fatal` is used and replace them with appropriate way. (returning error, using panic, just log error or ... etc)
  - For places where they are definitely needed, add `//nolint:forbidigo // reason` to avoid `forbidigo` linter which will be enabled in the next step.
- After replacing, enable `forbidigo` linter and configure it to forbid `os.Exit` and `klog.Fatal`.
  - also configure custom forbid reason messages described in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102231#issuecomment-1019274061)

What do you all think about this?

This will be related to `klog`. (Sorry if it's not appropriate sig)

/sig instrumentation
